title: Counting the Days Not Taken on an Interrupted Journey
content:
The days not taken on an interruption claim under the Travel Protection Plans are counted from a day that
depends on what the policy's claim record and the carrier's ledger of air bookings under the Air Ticket Fare Brands show between them: whether a delay head stands decided on the claim, and whether the carrier charged a
fare for an earlier return home on an airline cancellation.

## The three readings

1. Where a delay head stands decided on the claim record and the carrier's ledger carries a fare charged for an
   earlier return home raised on an airline cancellation, the days not taken are counted from the day that
   earlier return was bought to the last date of the journey, both counted.
2. Where a delay head stands decided on the claim record and the carrier's ledger carries no such fare, the days
   not taken are counted from the day after the journey was broken into to its last date, the last date counted.
3. In every other case the days not taken are counted from the day the journey was broken into to its last date,
   both counted.

The day the journey was broken into is the incident date standing on the claim the insurer decided last and
allowed on this policy.

## The counts compared on hypothetical dates

A journey ends on the 15th and was broken into on the 11th, an earlier return home having been bought on the
9th. Under the first reading the count runs from the 9th to the 15th, both counted, and comes to 7 days. Under
the second it runs from the 12th to the 15th, the last date counted, and comes to 4 days. Under the third it
runs from the 11th to the 15th, both counted, and comes to 5 days. The dates are hypothetical, and the three
counts differ in which day the count opens on and whether that opening day is itself counted.
